- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially after sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment > 0.7 → forecast overshoots true value by 5–15%).
- Forecasts show strong upward bias in early days of the 30-day horizon, then gradually flatten — true prices often dip or reverse after initial spike.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >95), model continues upward trend for 3–5 days, while true price often corrects or reverses within 7–10 days.
- Sentiment > 0.8 correlates with forecast overestimation; sentiment < 0.5 correlates with underestimation or early correction.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion after sustained highs; true prices often drop 5–10% from peak within 5–7 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows lag: true price often exceeds forecast by 2–4 days, especially when sentiment is positive and volatile.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.1 or below), model fails to adjust downward — true price drops sharply, often exceeding forecast by 10–20%.
- Model assumes linear continuation after spikes; true price often exhibits non-linear corrections or volatility clustering.
